analysis.title: FSA Fixed Income Daily Commentary - 19 November 2026
key_insights: US Treasuries rallied on 11/18 in a bull-flattening move: the 2-year was flat at 4.81% while the 10-year fell 3.7bp to 5.07% and the 30-year fell 4.8bp to 5.41%. The rally came despite hawkish FOMC minutes and was helped by a solid $16bn 20-year auction, lower oil and weaker equities.

The 20-year auction priced at a high yield of 5.459%, matching the when-issued yield. Bid-to-cover was 2.63x, in line with the prior six-auction average. Indirect bidders took 60.2%, direct 26.7% and primary dealers 13.1%.

FOMC minutes from the Oct 27-28 meeting showed almost all participants judged further rate increases would be needed. A couple of officials said a hike of more than 25bp in December could warrant consideration if inflation stays hot.

Fed Governor Waller called for a 50bp hike in December and said the Fed may need 100bp or more to 'shock' inflation out of the system. Barr said further hikes were likely appropriate. Daly urged a measured approach. Kashkari flagged AI investment concentration risk.

UK gilts rallied 8bp after October CPI came in slightly below the BoE's forecasts. Markets still price a 75% probability of a December BoE hike. Bailey warned more hikes would be needed the longer Middle East conflict keeps energy prices elevated.
UK October CPI rose 3.6% YoY from 3.5%, a one-year high, driven by fuel and energy. Services inflation was slightly softer than the BoE forecast.

WTI crude fell more than 3% and Brent fell 1.28% as hawkish Fed signals lifted the US dollar. EIA data showed US commercial crude inventories up 3.38 million barrels, above expectations, partly reflecting an SPR release.

US October housing starts rose 9.9% MoM to 1.309m annualized versus 1.25m consensus, on multifamily. Building permits fell 7.4% to 1.295m, a third straight monthly decline. Mortgage applications fell 2.3% in the week to Nov 13.

The US introduced restrictions limiting China's access to advanced AI chips and overseas computing capacity relying on US technology. China's Commerce Ministry opposed them and warned of countermeasures. This could complicate the trade truce ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting at APEC.
Bank Indonesia raised its policy rate 25bp to 6.00% on Nov 18, the first hike since June, to defend the rupiah. The deposit facility rate went to 5.25% and the lending facility rate to 6.75%.

Mongolia's president announced he will resign amid misconduct allegations. Malaysia revised Q3 GDP up to 5.5% from 5.3% on AI-related investment. Japan's October trade deficit narrowed to JPY476.5bn, with imports up 21.6% and crude imports up more than 60%.

Mineral Resources (MINAU) upgraded to OP from MP. It plans to use proceeds of the POSCO lithium deal ($765m gross, expected 1H FY2027) to redeem the remaining $750m of 9.25% notes due Oct 2028. Completion would cut weighted average cost of debt to about 6.9% and save roughly A$100m a year in interest. Execution risk remains because the deal is conditional and has already been delayed.

Hlth & Happiness (BTSDF) stays MP after a Moody's upgrade to Ba2 from Ba3 on Nov 18. Net leverage was 2.05x at June 30 versus 3.45x at FY25, 9M26 revenue rose 24.5%, and pet nutrition revenue fell 3.6%.

Cathay Life (CATLIF) cut to MP from UP. October after-tax profit fell 70.3% YoY to TWD4.4bn on AI-related equity valuation pressure, while 10M26 profit rose 31.1% to TWD64.5bn. Fubon 5.45% 12/10/35 is preferred over Cathay with a 10-20bp yield pick-up.

Nan Shan Life (NSINTW) stays MP after an October net loss of TWD3.9bn on FVTPL valuation losses, with 10M26 net income up 54.3% to TWD39.3bn. Nan Shan 5.875% 03/17/41 is preferred over Shin Kong. The 40bp spread gap to CATLIF is viewed as justified.

Indonesia (INDON) stays UP (underweight) on rupiah weakness of almost 10% YTD, a record low near IDR18,285, political turmoil after the VP resigned Nov 12, and 10-year yields near 7.62%. Reserves are $146.8bn. FSA sees 30-60bp spread pick-up in quasi-sovereigns PLNIJ and PERTIJ and turns MP on selective bonds.

NOVA Chemicals (NCX) stays MP. Q3 EBITDA was $392m, up 113% YoY but down 35% QoQ, with about $350m free cash flow. The $1,050m 5.25% 2027 notes are the main maturity risk, and $400m of 8.50% 2028 secured notes were called at 102.125%.

Target (TGT) initiated at MP. Q3 sales rose 7.1% to $27.07bn with comps +5.6%. Adjusted EPS was $2.65, including $0.50 from tariff refunds. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $10.65-$11.40. Net debt/EBITDA is 1.43x.

Lowe's (LOW) stays MP with a credit-neutral view. Q3 sales rose 9.3% to $22.8bn and comps rose 1.8% versus 0.1% consensus. Adjusted EPS of $3.10 included $0.34 from tariff refunds, or $2.76 excluding them. Gross margin fell 124bp and the adjusted operating margin outlook was cut to about 11.5%.

SSE (SSELN) stays MP. 1H FY27 adjusted operating profit rose 68% to GBP1.10bn, with transmission profit doubling to GBP584m. Free cash flow was negative GBP1.11bn on investment. FY27 EPS guidance of 168-193p and FY30 target of 225-250p were kept.

Eurobank (EUROB) stays MP. It is buying 65% of Bulgaria's Fibank for EUR0.65bn, taking about 160bp off CET1 to about 13.8% pro forma, with a roughly EUR750m equity raise. FSA views the deal as credit neutral.
BNP stays MP. The BNL 2030 plan targets pre-tax return on notional equity above 20% and cost/income of 56%. Group CET1 was 12.9% versus a 10.45% requirement, and a EUR1.3bn buyback was launched.
Woolworths (WOWAU) stays MP. Net debt/EBITDA was 2.5x at FY26 versus 2.8x. Operating capex is planned at about AUD2bn a year and the 70-75% payout policy was reaffirmed.

Occidental (OXY) stays OP. It launched cash tender offers for 16 note series with a USD500m cap per pool. Filling both caps would cut principal debt by about USD1.0bn to about USD8.95bn, from USD9.98bn, and a new USD6bn milestone was set.

Soquimich (SQM) stays MP. Q3 revenue rose 80% to $2.11bn but missed the $2.20bn consensus. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.03bn versus $1.10bn consensus. Net debt fell to $463m, or 0.1x EBITDA, and the company warned Q4 lithium prices could be substantially lower.
Israel Discount Bank (IDBILI) initiated at MP. Q3 net profit fell 20% to NIS910m with ROE of 10.4%, CET1 was 10.32%, and the Israel Credit Cards sale remains uncertain.

Tencent (TENCNT) stays MP after a recent upgrade, and FSA calls Q3 moderately credit-negative. Capex was RMB81.4bn versus RMB13.0bn a year earlier, free cash flow was negative RMB69.1bn, and net cash swung to RMB13.7bn net debt.

Sibanye-Stillwater (SSWSJ, OP) will redeem its $500m 4.125% 2028 convertible on Dec 21, 2026 at par. Conversion is open until Dec 11. The bonds trade near 160 and the conversion value is about 173. FSA prefers selling in the secondary market.

Cosan (CSANBZ) stays MP with a cautious bias. Holdco net debt is R$9.5bn, down 48% YoY, but DSCR is 0.3x with net dividends of R$507mn against R$1.71bn of net interest, so asset disposals remain necessary.
New Top Picks over the last 4 weeks are Sumitomo Life 5.308% 2056 (EUR), HSBC 7.625% PerpNC2031 (USD, YTC 7.29%) and ING 7.75% PerpNC2031 (USD, YTC 7.47%).

Remains OP on the credit. Cash tender offers for 16 note series would cut principal debt by about 10% if both caps are filled.
Remains MP. Q3 revenue and EBITDA missed consensus, net debt is 0.1x EBITDA, and management warned of lower Q4 lithium prices.

earnings_insights: Target 3Q26 (reported): net sales +7.1% YoY to $27.07bn, comps +5.6%, traffic +5.0%. Adjusted EPS $2.65 (+48.9%) includes $0.50 of tariff refunds. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $10.65-$11.40 from $9.90-$10.90.

Lowe's 3Q26 (reported 11/18): net sales $22.8bn vs consensus $22.4bn. Comps +1.8% vs consensus 0.1%. Adjusted EPS $3.10 vs consensus $2.88, including $0.34 of tariff refunds ($2.76 excluding them). Adjusted operating income $2.67bn vs consensus $2.55bn. FY26 adjusted EPS kept at about $12.25.
Soquimich 3Q26 (reported 11/17): revenue $2.11bn vs consensus $2.20bn, adjusted EBITDA $1.03bn vs consensus $1.10bn, net income $544m vs consensus $556m, all misses.
SSE 1H FY27 (reported 11/18): adjusted EPS 66.5p, within the 64-68p range indicated Oct 1. Adjusted operating profit GBP1.10bn.
NOVA Chemicals 3Q26 (reported): revenue $1,179m, EBITDA $392m, net income $48m.
Tencent 3Q26 (reported): revenue RMB207.3bn (+8%), non-IFRS operating profit RMB68.1bn (-6%), adjusted EBITDA RMB84.9bn (-2%).
Cathay Life October profit TWD4.4bn (-70.3% YoY), 10M26 TWD64.5bn (+31.1%). Nan Shan October loss TWD3.9bn, 10M26 net income TWD39.3bn (+54.3%).
Israel Discount Bank 3Q26 (reported): net profit NIS910m (-20% YoY), ROE 10.4%.
Cosan 3Q26 (reported): net profit R$190mn versus a R$1.2bn loss a year earlier. Compass EBITDA +22% to R$1.64bn, Rumo EBITDA -4% to R$2.22bn.

A one-year high on fuel and energy, but slightly below BoE forecasts, which cooled hike expectations.
Above the 1.25m consensus on multifamily rebound.
Consensus the print was measured against.
Third straight monthly decline, so starts could soften.
Waller's stated preference. The minutes say a hike above 25bp could be considered.
Market pricing after the UK CPI print.
Raised 25bp to defend the rupiah, the first hike since June.
Narrowed from JPY556.5bn, with oil imports up more than 60%.
Supported by AI investment and domestic demand.

trade_ideas.description: Sell the Sibanye-Stillwater 4.125% 2028 convertible (XS2725834043) in the secondary market near 160 ahead of the Dec 11 conversion deadline, or convert into shares.
trade_ideas.rationale: The bonds trade well above the par redemption price. Selling avoids equity volatility and conversion complexity.
trade_ideas.risk: Conversion value depends on share price, FX and execution costs. Letting the bonds be redeemed at par would crystallise a substantial loss.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Fubon 5.45% 12/10/35 over Cathay Life bonds for a 10-20bp yield pick-up, and Nan Shan 5.875% 03/17/41 over Shin Kong.
trade_ideas.rationale: Relative value among Taiwan lifers based on credit profile and risk-return balance.

trade_ideas.description: Turn MP on selective PLNIJ and PERTIJ bonds trading a bit too wide versus the INDON curve, for a 30-60bp spread pick-up.
trade_ideas.rationale: Quasi-sovereign bonds offer attractive spread pick-up over the sovereign curve.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening: almost all FOMC participants see more hikes, and some would consider more than 25bp in December.
Energy prices elevated by the Middle East conflict keep inflation pressure on the BoE and others.
Execution risk on Mineral Resources' POSCO deal, which is conditional and has been delayed.
Tencent's AI capex is eroding free cash flow and net cash.
Taiwan lifers face earnings volatility from equity market and FVTPL valuation swings tied to AI-related stocks.
Indonesian rupiah weakness, political uncertainty and elevated yields near post-pandemic highs.
Cosan's holdco DSCR of 0.3x leaves it dependent on asset disposals.
NOVA Chemicals' $1,050m 2027 maturity wall and short-dated securitization facilities.
US-China chip restrictions could complicate the trade truce.
vol_and_positioning: The Treasury rally came with weaker equity risk appetite: S&P 500 -1.02% on the day and -3.85% over the week, Nasdaq -0.74% on the day and -4.05% over the week.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict is keeping energy prices elevated, per BoE Governor Bailey, and raising Japan's crude import bill.
US restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips and overseas computing capacity. China's Commerce Ministry warned of countermeasures.
Trump held talks with Philippine President Marcos in Manila and announced a trade deal, then headed to Shenzhen to meet Xi Jinping.
Mongolian President Khurelsukh announced he will resign amid misconduct allegations.
Indonesian Vice President Gibran resigned on Nov 12 amid a wiretapping scandal and government infighting.

tension_points.bull_case: Longer-dated Treasuries rallied in a bull-flattening move, helped by a solid 20-year auction (bid-to-cover 2.63x, in line with average), lower oil and weaker equity risk appetite.
tension_points.bear_case: FOMC minutes showed almost all participants expect more hikes, a couple would consider more than 25bp in December, and Waller called for 50bp. The tightening cycle is not complete.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation data deteriorating, which the minutes say could make policy more aggressive than 25bp in December.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth accelerated to 5.47% in Q3, inflation is inside the 2.5% plus or minus 1% target, reserves are $146.8bn, and the fiscal deficit is 1.47% of GDP through October.
tension_points.bear_case: The rupiah is near a record low, political uncertainty followed the VP's resignation, 10-year yields are near post-pandemic highs, and the full-year deficit is projected at 2.85% of GDP against the 3% ceiling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further rupiah weakness or political turmoil that delays policy decisions and raises the risk premium.
